environment: Apple M4 / Darwin arm64 / Go 1.27.3 / GOMAXPROCS4, unprofiled latency experiments. Local start load average 2.57 / 1.58 / 1.34; other workloads were not stopped.
implementation: Only the FP32 remainder-row path changes: reuse each input element for two distinct output accumulators, keeping ascending input-index accumulation order for each output, and use the original scalar tail for odd output counts. Four-row prefill arithmetic, output tiles, work threshold, workers, executor borrowing/join rules and quantized kernels remain unchanged. No new unsafe code, dependencies, invocation state or allocations.
correctness: 630 row/column/output combinations cover zero dimensions, rows 1/2/3/4/5/7/8/9/17 and 31/32/33/63/65 output boundaries, comparing frozen, experimental and production ranges. Ten larger serial/parallel invocation cases check bit identity, zero warm allocations and post-join state cleanup. Signed zero, subnormal, infinities and NaN payload patterns match reference bits. Existing normal and race full suites and complete generation equality pass. Call sites use distinct input/output buffers; no in-place matmul support is introduced.

kernel.description: Frozen single-output range versus paired-output experiment, with matched reusable runner/callback dispatch on both sides. Balanced AB/BA blocks; calls per block max(1, 2^22/(rows*columns*outputs)). Three fresh processes; all warm allocation counts zero. Test/prototype and executable hashes pinned in each receipt. These were measured before production integration, against baseline runtime c8503a2e.
kernel.interpretation: Decode/remainder-row cases show substantial reductions, but four-row controls and mixed 5-row parallel cases retain slower observations. Do not claim universal kernel improvement or prefill non-regression.

generation.interpretation: Complete before/after runtimes share a binary, three processes and 48 alternating pairs per shape. All warm and timed completion JSONs match outside timing. The old c8503a2e identical-runtime control binary was freshly rerun, not rebuilt as candidate self/self: its build receipt predates this experiment and records source/driver/binary bindings. Both experiments use Go1.27.3 and the same generation driver. Synthetic model dimensions256/hidden704/layer1, greedy no-EOS sampling. Observed 128-output latency falls around31-32%, with old-self control around1.000-1.001. Short prompt/one-output and eight-output cases also improve. Long-prefill/one-output differences are much smaller and should not be generalized. No real-model, other-OS/toolchain, quantized throughput, tail-latency, RSS or universal no-regression claim.

decision: Retain the paired-output path as a promising local FP32 compute candidate; substantially larger complete-generation differences than measured self controls support further review. Not merged, committed or pushed as part of this experiment. Require broader platform/toolchain/model validation before universal claims.
